reason: Credit support to AI cloud partners is a programme within q09's total of financing commitments and capacity backstops, and both are checked as an amount outstanding in the same FY2027 10-K, so under boundary 1 (R2-e) the part does not separate them.

Both ask whether NVIDIA signs a guarantee or backstop of OpenAI's Ohio data-center lease; the end-2027 check date is another deadline for the same signing (boundary 2), and the amount is a detail of that one deal, not a separate check.
Both ask whether the Vera Rubin generation starts shipping by the end of calendar 2026.
Whether the big four hyperscalers' combined calendar-2027 data-center capex reaches $1 trillion is settled by the same reported figure q13 asks for.

It bundles NAND prices, 2026 price levels and the per-rack memory cost with the DRAM/HBM trend, and each of these is its own check that can move apart from q05's single figure, the 2027-versus-2026 change in server DRAM and HBM contract prices.
Whether Kyber NVL144 Rubin Ultra racks first ship in 2027 or slip to 2028 is settled by q18's yes or no on shipping by 31 December 2027.

Supply and purchase commitments to suppliers (the $119 billion) are a separate 10-K total from q09's financing commitments and backstops to customers and partners, and the two can move apart; they share only any capacity NVIDIA agrees to buy back from partners.

Same year and the same custom-chip programmes, but it asks the revenue the four hyperscalers' in-house accelerators earn, or their shipment volume, as the four disclose it, while q16 asks all cloud providers' dollar spending on custom ASICs, so different figures settle the two.

Domestic products' share of Chinese enterprise accelerator budgets over the 12 months from July 2026, per a follow-up survey, is a different measure and period from NVIDIA's share of China's calendar-2026 data-center accelerator spending, though the two move against each other.
No reference question asks about a US ban on Chinese-made lidar sensors.
Both ask whether Chinese authorities approve imports of Nvidia H200 chips by the end of January 2027; the approved quantity is a detail of that same approval and does not resolve on its own.
No reference question asks about the French competition authority's antitrust investigation of Nvidia.
